title: Class diagram on ELK: Mermaid's handover order, multiplicities as ELK end labels, three departures

v:
## Context

The class diagram moves onto the shared ELK layout core (`layout/directedGraph/`), the second kind after the flowchart (`01M4VA67HYZZ1PZG49XA30454N`), under the rules of `01M4VANRC6B2C14NHVC2KRZ9Y8`. A class diagram brings one thing the flowchart does not have: the multiplicities written at a relationship's two ends (`Customer "1" --> "*" Order`). Mermaid 12.2.0 hands them to ELK and repairs their places afterwards; the core had no such capability.

What Mermaid 12.2.0 does, read in its dist (`node_modules/.pnpm/mermaid@12.2.0/node_modules/mermaid/dist/chunks/mermaid.esm/`) and measured in headless Chrome:

- **Handover order.** `ClassDB.getData` (`classDiagram-v2-K6ZTA64I.mjs`, line 1808) lists every namespace, then every class in first-mention order, then every note, then every lollipop interface; its edges are the note links (from the note to the class) and then the relations. ELK keeps model order. Measured: `class X`, `namespace N1 { P }`, `namespace N2 { Q }`, `class Y` draws N1, N2, X, Y left to right; `A --> B` with `note for B` under TB draws the note a layer above B.
- **Namespace frames.** A namespace is an ELK compound node, like a subgraph (`buildSubgraphLayoutOptions`, `elk-V4PLJRSU.mjs` around line 99284), its title centred across the top.
- **Connectors.** Every edge ELK routed, relations and note links alike, is drawn `rounded` (`applyElkEdgeLayout`, line 100402), with line hops.
- **Multiplicities.** The from end's is `startLabelRight`, the to end's `endLabelLeft` (`classDiagram-v2-K6ZTA64I.mjs`, line 1910). `terminalElkLabels` (`elk-V4PLJRSU.mjs`, line 99827) hands each to ELK as an edge label placed `TAIL` or `HEAD`, grown by 6px on every side where that end carries a marker. After layout, `slideTerminalLabelsOffFrames` (line 100547) slides a label lying across a frame along the segment it sits beside until it is clear of every obstacle (`terminalLabelObstacles`, line 100479) and 2px clear of frames; `putTerminalLabelsOnTheirSide` (line 100580) mirrors a label onto its own hand of the line (a `…Right` label right of the direction of travel, a `…Left` one left of it) when the mirrored place is clear.

## Decision

The class adapter (`layoutClassDiagram`) hands the core namespaces as clusters (12px padding, the title's measured size), classes, notes and lollipop labels in Mermaid's order, note links from the note to the class, then relations; every connector carries the `rounded` corner radius for the line hops. It hands each multiplicity as a terminal label: `startRight` for the from end, `endLeft` for the to end, measured at the 12px it is drawn at, with a 6px margin where that end draws a marker. The core gained terminal labels (`terminalLabels` in, `terminalLabelCenters` out) and ports `terminalElkLabels`, `slideTerminalLabelsOffFrames`, `putTerminalLabelsOnTheirSide` and `terminalLabelObstacles` into `placeTerminalLabels`. Mermaid's `followMovedEndpoints` is not ported: it follows route ends that Mermaid moves after layout for its markers, and the core moves no route end.

Three departures from Mermaid 12, under rule 1 of `01M4VANRC6B2C14NHVC2KRZ9Y8`:

1. **A label struck by any obstacle slides, not only one across a frame; with no clear place on its own side, the other side is tried.** ELK keeps room for an end label beside its end, but not clear of a neighbouring edge leaving the same side. Measured with the class adapter: `Keeper "1" --> "*" Animal` beside `Keeper -- Habitat` and `Habitat --* Animal` draws "*" across Habitat's line under TB and "1" across it under LR, where the neighbouring line runs alongside the whole segment, so sliding alone finds no place. A multiplicity on another relationship's line reads as that line's. Over the class parity fixtures and that document in all four directions (26 multiplicities, a canvas-like measurer), Mermaid's rule leaves 3 struck by a line or a class box; Siren's leaves 0. On the four class parity fixtures alone both leave 0, and the parity numbers do not move.
2. **An edge handed to ELK turned round keeps its labels at its own ends.** `subgraphFeedbackEdges` (Mermaid's `reverseSubgraphFeedbackEdges`) swaps an edge's ends for ELK; Mermaid leaves the labels' `TAIL`/`HEAD` as they were, so a multiplicity on a turned edge lands at the other class. The core swaps the placement with the ends. Core test: "keeps each label at its own end of an edge handed to ELK turned round".
3. **Terminal labels block a cluster's title** (`placeTitlesClear`, decision `01M4VFW4XGRGSMTMQ12HME145W`), as route segments do. That decision's "Edge labels" section found no centre label in a band and asked for a recheck when end labels arrived. They do land there: an end inside the frame puts its label beside it, up in the band. Over 20,000 random small graphs (one titled cluster, 2 to 4 boxes, TB and LR, both ends of every edge labelled), labels overlapping the title fell from 262 to 106 with labels blocking it. The remaining 106 are bands with no room beside the labels, where the title stays centred, as it does for routes. The class parity fixtures have no label on a title either way. Core test: "keeps a cluster's title off the terminal labels in its band, where the band has room".

The namespace frame uses its own 12px padding, not Mermaid's 24px, for the reasons in `01M4VDB3XG71N3R1EN5J94JMZ4`.

## Evidence

Gate (rule 8 of `01M4VANRC6B2C14NHVC2KRZ9Y8`), parity over the three committed class fixtures (`example-class-core`, `example-class-structure`, `example-class-full`), Siren on ELK against Mermaid 12.2.0 default in headless Chrome:

| Measure | Siren on ELK | Mermaid | Gate |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Through unrelated boxes | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| Crossings | 0 | 0 | at most 110% of Mermaid's |
| Vertical agreement (pooled, 74 pairs) | 97.3% | | at least 90% |
| Horizontal agreement (pooled) | 100.0% | | at least 90% |
| Failures | 0 | | 0 |

On a wider set that also held one larger local document, the same run went from dagre (3 edges through boxes, 4 crossings, 53.6% / 77.8% agreement) to ELK (0, 0, 97.4% / 100.0%), with through-titles 0, reversals 5 against Mermaid's 5 and mean detour 1.23 against 1.22.

The gate passes. The 11 flowchart fixtures are unchanged: crossings 176 against 176, vertical 99.6%, horizontal 97.8%, through-nodes 0, through-titles 15.

## Consequences

Every class diagram's picture changes: orthogonal rounded connectors with line hops, frames from the engine, notes laid out a layer before their class, namespaces before the classes outside them. A multiplicity sits beside its own end, on its own hand of the line where that is clear. State and ER diagrams get terminal labels from the same core when they move.
